items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: In Figure 4, probenecid and allopurinol both lower serum uric acid, but through different mechanisms. What is the key difference?

options.A: Probenecid increases renal excretion of uric acid; allopurinol decreases uric acid production
options.C: Probenecid decreases uric acid production; allopurinol increases renal excretion
options.D: Neither drug affects serum uric acid levels

items.why: Figure 4 shows allopurinol (and febuxostat) acting as xanthine oxidase inhibitors that reduce uric acid production, while probenecid acts at the kidney to increase renal excretion of uric acid that has already been produced — two different strategies for the same goal of lowering serum uric acid.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient presents with an acute gout flare. Which action is most appropriate at this visit?

options.A: Treat the acute flare (colchicine, NSAID, or corticosteroid) and defer urate-lowering therapy
options.B: Start allopurinol immediately to lower uric acid
options.C: Start febuxostat and allopurinol together
options.D: No treatment is needed until uric acid is measured

items.why: Starting or changing urate-lowering therapy during an acute flare can worsen or prolong it. Treat the flare first; urate-lowering therapy is started or adjusted only once it resolves.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: In Figure 5, which agent is the odd one out, acting directly on the skeletal muscle fiber rather than within the central nervous system?

options.C: Baclofen

items.why: Dantrolene decreases calcium release from the skeletal muscle sarcoplasmic reticulum, acting directly on the muscle fiber — unlike cyclobenzaprine, tizanidine, and baclofen, which all act within the CNS to reduce excitatory output to motor neurons.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Which skeletal muscle relaxant acts directly on skeletal muscle itself (not the CNS), making it the agent of choice in malignant hyperthermia?

options.C: Tizanidine

items.why: Dantrolene’s peripheral mechanism — decreasing calcium release from the skeletal muscle sarcoplasmic reticulum — is unique among these agents and is exactly why it is the emergency treatment for malignant hyperthermia.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: In Figure 6, PTH release raises serum calcium through three parallel actions. Which organ system is NOT one of the three direct targets of PTH shown in the diagram?

options.C: Intestine (directly)

items.why: PTH acts directly on bone (↑ osteoclast resorption) and kidney (↑ calcium reabsorption, activates vitamin D); its effect on the intestine is indirect, mediated through activated vitamin D. The lung is not part of this feedback loop at all.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Based on Figure 7, which bisphosphonate requires the fewest doses per year, and by what route is it given?

options.C: All bisphosphonates require the same number of annual doses

items.why: Figure 7 shows zoledronic acid dosed as infrequently as once yearly by IV infusion, versus weekly oral dosing for alendronate/risedronate and monthly oral dosing for ibandronate — an important consideration for patients with adherence challenges.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: In Figure 8, teriparatide and romosozumab sit on the "bone formation" side of the balance, while alendronate and raloxifene sit on the "bone resorption" side. What does this grouping represent?

options.A: Teriparatide and romosozumab stimulate osteoblast activity, while alendronate and raloxifene inhibit osteoclast activity
options.B: All four drugs work through the identical mechanism
options.C: Teriparatide and romosozumab inhibit osteoclasts, while alendronate and raloxifene stimulate osteoblasts
options.D: This grouping reflects route of administration, not mechanism

items.why: The "anabolic" agents (teriparatide, abaloparatide, romosozumab) sit on the bone-formation side because they stimulate osteoblasts, while bisphosphonates (alendronate), denosumab, SERMs (raloxifene), and calcitonin sit on the bone-resorption side because they inhibit osteoclasts — two different strategies for shifting the same remodeling balance.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient is counseled to take their oral bisphosphonate with a full glass of water and remain upright for a specified period. What complication is this counseling primarily meant to prevent?

options.C: Esophageal irritation or injury

items.why: Taking the tablet with a full glass of water and staying upright reduces the time the pill is in contact with the esophageal mucosa, lowering the risk of esophageal irritation or injury.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient with osteoporosis has significant difficulty swallowing pills. Which administration route among osteoporosis therapies would best fit this patient?

options.C: There is no alternative to oral bisphosphonates
options.D: Yearly IV zoledronic acid or a subcutaneous injectable agent

items.why: Route of administration and adherence are explicit factors in choosing osteoporosis therapy — IV zoledronic acid or an injectable agent (e.g., denosumab) avoids the swallowing difficulty that limits oral options.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Why is acetaminophen not a reliable first-line choice for an inflammatory joint flare, despite being a good analgesic/antipyretic?

options.B: It has minimal peripheral anti-inflammatory effect
options.C: It is contraindicated in all patients with joint pain
options.D: It is a DMARD and too strong for mild flares

items.why: Acetaminophen has minimal peripheral anti-inflammatory effect, unlike NSAIDs — it treats pain and fever, not inflammation itself.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A 70-year-old with CKD and heart failure needs osteoarthritis pain control. Considering systemic risk, which is generally the safest starting point?

options.C: Acetaminophen or a topical NSAID

items.why: Acetaminophen or a topical NSAID avoids the systemic renal/CV risk of oral NSAIDs in a patient with CKD and heart failure.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Which pairing correctly matches a drug with its primary mechanism?

options.C: Baclofen — calcium channel blockade in skeletal muscle

items.why: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase. Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase; colchicine disrupts microtubules; baclofen is a GABA-B agonist.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient on a biologic DMARD develops a fever. What is the most important immediate concern?

options.A: Infection, given the drug’s immunosuppressive effect
options.C: Osteonecrosis of the jaw

items.why: Immunosuppression is the shared major risk across all DMARDs — a fever must be treated as a possible infection until proven otherwise.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Which statement about gout pharmacology is correct?

options.B: Acute flares should always be treated with urate-lowering therapy first
options.C: Probenecid lowers uric acid by inhibiting renal tubular reabsorption of urate
options.D: Febuxostat and probenecid are both xanthine oxidase inhibitors

items.why: Probenecid is a uricosuric agent that inhibits renal tubular reabsorption of uric acid, increasing its excretion. Colchicine does not lower uric acid; febuxostat (not probenecid) is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor; and urate-lowering therapy is deferred during an acute flare.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient with glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis risk should be counseled that the risk is primarily related to which mechanism?

options.A: Increased osteoclast-mediated resorption and decreased bone formation
options.C: Excess vitamin D

items.why: Glucocorticoids increase osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and suppress osteoblast-driven bone formation — shifting the remodeling balance toward bone loss.

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: How does colchicine relieve an acute gout flare?

options.A: It disrupts microtubules, reducing neutrophil migration
options.B: It blocks phospholipase A₂ upstream of COX
options.C: It converts uric acid to allantoin in the joint
options.D: It blocks URAT1, increasing uric acid excretion
options.E: It inhibits xanthine oxidase, lowering uric acid

items.why: Colchicine binds tubulin and blocks microtubule polymerization, reducing neutrophil migration and NLRP3 activation (S10; S11; SG U2-M).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient on colchicine for a gout flare is prescribed clarithromycin for pneumonia. What is the concern?

options.A: Clarithromycin speeds colchicine clearance, so the flare returns
options.C: CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition raises colchicine to toxic levels
options.D: The pair raises uric acid and worsens the flare
options.E: The two together cause hemolysis in G6PD deficiency

items.why: CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors such as clarithromycin, cyclosporine, and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors raise colchicine toxicity (S11).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient of Han Chinese descent with recurrent gout is about to start allopurinol. Which pre-treatment step does the lecture tie to Lecture 1’s pharmacogenomics?

options.A: G6PD testing for hemolysis risk on the drug
options.B: HLA-B*58:01 testing for severe hypersensitivity risk
options.C: TPMT testing for bone marrow toxicity risk
options.D: CYP2D6 genotyping for poor metabolizer status
options.E: Baseline joint aspiration for urate crystals

items.why: The HLA-B*58:01 allele raises the risk of severe cutaneous/hypersensitivity reactions to allopurinol (S12; S13); the textbook recommends screening in Han Chinese, Korean, and Thai patients (p. 696).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient with refractory tophaceous gout is being considered for pegloticase. Which test must come first?

options.C: A 24-hour urine urate, to rule out stones
options.E: G6PD activity, because of hemolysis risk

items.why: Pegloticase and rasburicase are contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (hemolysis risk) (S15).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient with gout and CKD stage 3 is starting allopurinol. Which textbook starting dose fits?

options.A: Allopurinol is not used at all in CKD
options.B: 300 mg/d from day one to reach target fast
options.C: 100 mg/d, the same as normal kidney function
options.D: No more than 50 mg/d, titrated by 50 mg

items.why: In chronic kidney disease the initial allopurinol dose should not exceed 50 mg/d, with 50-mg titrations (p. 695).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: During general anesthesia with a volatile agent and succinylcholine, a patient develops rising temperature, rigidity, and acidosis. Which drug is the emergency treatment, and where does it act?

options.A: Baclofen, activating GABA-B receptors in the cord
options.C: Dantrolene, blocking RyR1 calcium release in muscle

items.why: Malignant hyperthermia is triggered by volatile anesthetics and succinylcholine; dantrolene blocks RyR1 so less calcium leaves the sarcoplasmic reticulum (S34; S35; SG U2-R11).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient with multiple sclerosis has an intrathecal baclofen pump. The pump runs dry over a holiday weekend. What should the team anticipate?

options.A: Serotonin syndrome from loss of 5-HT2 block
options.B: No change, since baclofen has a long half-life
options.C: Withdrawal: seizures, hyperthermia, rebound spasticity
options.D: Rebound hypertension from loss of α2 action

items.why: Abrupt discontinuation, especially intrathecal, can cause a dangerous withdrawal syndrome with seizures, hyperthermia, and rebound spasticity (S27; S28).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient taking tizanidine for spasticity is prescribed ciprofloxacin for a urinary infection. What is the problem?

options.A: Ciprofloxacin blocks RyR1 and adds weakness
options.C: Ciprofloxacin induces CYP1A2, so spasticity returns
options.E: CYP1A2 inhibition sharply raises tizanidine levels

items.why: Ciprofloxacin and fluvoxamine strongly raise tizanidine levels via CYP1A2 — the combination is contraindicated (S30).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A 78-year-old asks for cyclobenzaprine for back spasm. Which concern is most specific to this drug in an older adult?

options.C: Seizures on abrupt withdrawal of a pump
options.E: Hemolysis in a patient with G6PD deficiency

items.why: Cyclobenzaprine is tricyclic-like: dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention, confusion — on the Beers list in older adults; short-term use only (S31; S32).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Which agent is a Schedule IV controlled substance because it is metabolized to meprobamate?

options.C: Tizanidine

items.why: Carisoprodol is metabolized to meprobamate and is a Schedule IV controlled substance with dependence/misuse potential (S33).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A young man with extensive burns needs emergency intubation. Why is succinylcholine avoided?

options.A: It lasts many hours in burned patients
options.B: Potassium release can cause cardiac arrest
options.C: It cannot reach the burned muscle tissue
options.D: Burns make it a nondepolarizing blocker
options.E: It is reversed too quickly by sugammadex

items.why: Burns and denervation proliferate extrajunctional receptors; succinylcholine then releases potassium, which can cause cardiac arrest (p. 508).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A 66-year-old woman starts weekly alendronate. Which counseling point most reduces her risk of esophageal injury?

options.A: Take it with breakfast to protect the stomach
options.B: Take it at bedtime with a calcium supplement
options.C: Lie down for 30 minutes after the dose
options.D: Take it with coffee to speed gastric emptying
options.E: Full glass of plain water, then stay upright 30 minutes

items.why: Take with a full glass of water first thing in the morning, fasting, and remain upright — this reduces esophageal contact time and irritation (S52; S53; SG U2-R13).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Which option correctly describes the PTH feedback loop?

options.A: Low calcium → vitamin D → PTH suppression and calcium excretion
options.B: High calcium → PTH → bone formation, renal excretion, less gut absorption
options.C: Low calcium → PTH → bone resorption, renal reabsorption, vitamin D gut absorption
options.D: Low calcium → calcitonin → bone resorption and renal reabsorption
options.E: Low calcium → PTH → osteoblast-only bone formation

items.why: Falling calcium triggers PTH, which raises calcium via bone resorption, renal reabsorption, and (via vitamin D activation) intestinal absorption (S43; SG U2-R12).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Which osteoporosis drug is an anabolic PTH analog that stimulates osteoblast bone formation?

options.C: Alendronate

items.why: Teriparatide (PTH 1-34, daily injection) is an anabolic agent that stimulates osteoblasts and new bone formation (S54; S55; SG U2-M).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient on denosumab for 4 years wants to stop it because of the injections. What should the PA advise?

options.B: Take a drug holiday, as for bisphosphonates
options.C: Switch to teriparatide for life
options.D: Don’t just stop — transition to a bisphosphonate
options.E: Stop safely: its effect lasts years in bone

items.why: Denosumab discontinuation causes rebound vertebral fractures; transition to a bisphosphonate (S55).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A 70-year-old with a myocardial infarction 6 months ago has severe osteoporosis. Which agent should be avoided because of its boxed warning?

options.C: Alendronate

items.why: Romosozumab carries a boxed warning for MI, stroke, and cardiovascular death (S55).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A patient with CrCl 25 mL/min has osteoporosis. Which drug class is contraindicated at this kidney function?

options.C: Bisphosphonates such as alendronate

items.why: Bisphosphonates are contraindicated with severe renal impairment (CrCl below 30–35 mL/min) (S48); renal function is part of choosing therapy (S59).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: Why does raloxifene suit some patients with vertebral osteoporosis but not those whose main risk is hip fracture?

options.A: It is contraindicated in all women over 65
options.B: It must be stopped after 2 years
options.C: It builds new bone only in the hip
options.D: It raises hip fracture risk through VTE
options.E: It reduces spine fractures but not hip fractures

items.why: Raloxifene protects against spine fractures but not hip fractures, unlike bisphosphonates, denosumab, and teriparatide (p. 827).

items.label: Self-test question
items.stem: A 72-year-old with OA, CKD, hypertension, and an anticoagulant now has an acute gout flare. Which plan best fits the study guide?

options.B: Start febuxostat today to stop the flare
options.C: Probenecid now, since the kidneys are the issue
options.D: Full-dose oral naproxen; start allopurinol now

items.why: An oral NSAID is relatively contraindicated (CKD, anticoagulant, hypertension); a short corticosteroid course is often preferred, colchicine needs renal dose adjustment, and ULT waits until the flare resolves (SG U2-S).

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A 68-year-old woman with prior vertebral fractures and very high fracture risk is choosing therapy. What does the lecture suggest first?

options.A: An anabolic agent such as teriparatide
options.C: A drug holiday from all therapy

items.why: Higher-risk patients may need an anabolic agent first (then an antiresorptive); fracture history, renal function, and route also guide choice.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A transplant patient taking azathioprine develops gout and needs allopurinol. What must happen?

options.C: Stop azathioprine for one week
options.D: No change; there is no interaction

items.why: Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, which clears azathioprine and mercaptopurine — reduce their dose (textbook: by 75%).

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A patient taking sertraline is prescribed cyclobenzaprine for a back strain. What interaction should the PA flag?

options.C: Acute kidney injury

items.why: Cyclobenzaprine carries serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs, SNRIs, and tramadol; MAOIs are contraindicated.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A patient with gout and a history of uric acid kidney stones needs urate-lowering therapy. Which drug should be avoided?

options.C: Allopurinol

items.why: Probenecid raises urinary uric acid, so avoid it with uric acid kidney stones or significant renal impairment.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which effect explains glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis?

options.A: Excess vitamin D from the kidney
options.C: Excess calcitonin from the thyroid

items.why: Glucocorticoids increase osteoclast-mediated resorption and suppress osteoblast-driven formation, tipping the balance to bone loss.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which mechanism belongs to baclofen?

options.A: GABA-B agonism in the spinal cord
options.C: Central alpha-2 adrenergic agonism

items.why: Baclofen activates GABA-B receptors, causing presynaptic inhibition and less excitatory transmitter release.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: In a gout flare, what activates the inflammatory response once urate crystals form in the joint?

options.C: Osteoclasts via RANKL signaling
options.D: Neutrophils and macrophages via NLRP3 and IL-1β

items.why: Monosodium urate crystals activate neutrophils and macrophages through NLRP3 and IL-1β, producing the acute flare.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which osteoporosis drug is limited to 2 years of lifetime use and should be followed by an antiresorptive?

options.C: Denosumab

items.why: Teriparatide is limited to 2 years lifetime, then followed by an antiresorptive to keep the bone gained.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A patient starting weekly risedronate asks how to take it. Which instruction is correct?

options.A: With an antacid to protect the stomach
options.B: At bedtime, then lie down to rest
options.C: Fasting, full glass of water, upright 30 minutes
options.D: With breakfast and a calcium tablet
options.E: With coffee to help it absorb

items.why: Take it first thing in the morning, fasting, with a full glass of plain water, and stay upright for 30 minutes to limit esophageal irritation.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A patient on tizanidine reports dizziness on standing and has new elevated liver enzymes. Which pair of effects is typical of tizanidine?

options.C: Hemolysis and infusion reactions

items.why: Tizanidine causes sedation, hypotension/bradycardia, dry mouth, and hepatotoxicity — monitor LFTs.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which drug blocks osteoclast formation by inhibiting RANKL?

options.C: Teriparatide

items.why: Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody against RANKL that blocks osteoclast formation (it mimics OPG).

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: In the OR, after sevoflurane and succinylcholine, a patient’s end-tidal CO₂ and temperature climb with jaw rigidity. Which drug is given IV now?

options.C: Dantrolene

items.why: Malignant hyperthermia (volatile anesthetics, succinylcholine) is treated with IV dantrolene, which blocks RyR1 calcium release.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A woman with a past DVT asks about raloxifene for osteoporosis. What is the key concern?

options.B: It causes osteonecrosis of the jaw
options.C: It carries a boxed MI and stroke warning
options.D: It must be taken upright with water

items.why: Raloxifene raises VTE risk (and causes hot flashes), though it may reduce breast cancer risk.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which drug lowers serum uric acid by increasing its renal excretion?

options.C: Probenecid

items.why: Probenecid is a uricosuric: it blocks URAT1-mediated tubular reabsorption, so excretion rises.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: What distinguishes dantrolene from cyclobenzaprine, tizanidine, and baclofen?

options.A: It acts on GABA-B receptors in the cord
options.B: It is a central alpha-2 agonist
options.C: It blocks ACh release at the junction
options.D: It acts in the brainstem on 5-HT2
options.E: It acts on the muscle fiber, not the CNS

items.why: Dantrolene decreases calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (RyR1) inside the muscle fiber; the others act in the CNS.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A patient’s first gout flare settled two weeks ago; uric acid remains high and flares are recurring. What is the best next step?

options.A: Give colchicine only until the next flare
options.B: Wait for the next flare before deciding
options.C: Start allopurinol low with colchicine prophylaxis
options.E: Start allopurinol at full dose with no prophylaxis

items.why: Once the flare resolves, start a xanthine oxidase inhibitor low, titrate to a urate target, and give colchicine or an NSAID prophylaxis for 3–6 months.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Falling serum calcium triggers PTH release. Which set lists PTH’s three ways of raising calcium?

options.B: Bone resorption, renal reabsorption, vitamin D gut absorption
options.C: Renal excretion, osteoblast growth, insulin release
options.D: Bone formation, renal excretion, gut secretion
options.E: Gut secretion, bone formation, vitamin D breakdown

items.why: PTH raises calcium via bone resorption, renal reabsorption, and (via vitamin D activation) intestinal absorption.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which urate-lowering drug carries a boxed warning for cardiovascular death?

options.C: Allopurinol

items.why: Febuxostat carries a boxed warning for cardiovascular death (the textbook notes later data were reassuring; answer with the slides).

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes spasticity from rigidity?

options.A: Spasticity is a sudden involuntary contraction
options.B: Spasticity is velocity-dependent; rigidity is not
options.C: Both respond to the same drugs
options.E: Rigidity is velocity-dependent; spasticity is not

items.why: Spasticity is velocity-dependent increased tone from upper motor neuron injury; rigidity is constant tone, independent of velocity.
